stem: Model Exam 4
Which of the following is the percentage of people who develop loss of vision due to orbital cellulitis?
Which of the following is the percentage of people who develop loss of vision due to orbital cellulitis?
explanation_verbatim: Vision loss due to orbital cellulitis most commonly falls within the range of 7-11 %. This occurs due to complications like optic neuritis, central retinal artery occlusion, or orbital abscesses, making early recognition and aggressive treatment essential to preserving vision.

stem: A 22-year-old female patient complains of hard dry scales around the bases of eyelashes. Examination revealed ulceration of lid margin and scarring of lashes. Which of the following is the causative organism of that patient's condition?

A 22-year-old female patient complains of hard dry scales around the bases of eyelashes. Examination revealed ulceration of lid margin and scarring of lashes. Which of the following is the causative organism of that patient's condition?
explanation_verbatim: Staphylococcal infection is the most common cause of ulcerative blepharitis, which presents with hard scales, lash loss, and lid margin scarring. It often results from chronic bacterial colonization of eyelid margins.

stem: All of the following can cause conjunctival papillae except?
All of the following can cause conjunctival papillae except?
explanation_verbatim: Papillae are caused by nonspecific conjunctival inflammation, typically due to allergy, foreign bodies, or contact lens irritation. Chlamydia causes follicles, not papillae.

stem: Which of the following conditions is described as a localized protrusion of the sclera lined by uveal tissue and appearing blue in color?
Which of the following conditions is described as a localized protrusion of the sclera lined by uveal tissue and appearing blue in color?
explanation_verbatim: A staphyloma is a localized blue-black bulging of the weakened sclera lined by uveal tissue. It occurs due to thinning of the sclera from inflammation or degeneration.

stem: Which of the following is best described as (tremulousness of the iris with eye movement)?
Which of the following is best described as (tremulousness of the iris with eye movement)?
explanation_verbatim: Iridodonesis means trembling of the iris during eye movement, usually due to absence of lens support (as in aphakia or subluxated lens). It indicates loss of zonular or lenticular stability.

stem: A 28-year-old female patient complains of ocular pain, excessive lacrimation together with diminished vision. Examination revealed keratic precipitates, hypopyon and ciliary injection with violaceous hue. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old female patient complains of ocular pain, excessive lacrimation together with diminished vision. Examination revealed keratic precipitates, hypopyon and ciliary injection with violaceous hue. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Iridocyclitis (anterior uveitis) presents with pain, photophobia, lacrimation, and keratic precipitates with ciliary congestion. It involves inflammation of the iris and ciliary body.

stem: A 28-year-old female patient complains of ocular pain, excessive lacrimation together with diminished vision. Examination revealed keratic precipitates, hypopyon and ciliary injection with violaceous hue. which of the Following is an expected complication?

A 28-year-old female patient complains of ocular pain, excessive lacrimation together with diminished vision. Examination revealed keratic precipitates, hypopyon and ciliary injection with violaceous hue. which of the Following is an expected complication?
explanation_verbatim: Chronic iridocyclitis may lead to posterior synechiae, secondary glaucoma, cataract formation, and band keratopathy due to prolonged inflammation.

stem: Which of the following is the most common intraocular malignancy in the adult age group?
Which of the following is the most common intraocular malignancy in the adult age group?
explanation_verbatim: Choroidal melanoma is the most common intraocular malignancy in adults. It arises from uveal melanocytes and may cause visual loss or retinal detachment.

stem: A 33-year-old female patient presents to the ophthalmologist with a painful red swelling localized over the medial canthal area. Which of the following is the most suitable diagnosis for such a swelling?

A 33-year-old female patient presents to the ophthalmologist with a painful red swelling localized over the medial canthal area. Which of the following is the most suitable diagnosis for such a swelling?
explanation_verbatim: A painful red swelling over the medial canthal area is characteristic of acute dacryocystitis, which is inflammation of the lacrimal sac due to nasolacrimal duct obstruction. It typically presents with localized tenderness, redness, and swelling below the medial canthus, often with purulent discharge.

stem: A 2-year-old child with esotropia and amblyopia. What is the most appropriate management for that child?
options: Full cycloplegic correction with eye patching

stem: A 2-year-old child with esotropia and amblyopia. What is the most appropriate management for that child?
options: Full cycloplegic correction with eye patching
explanation_verbatim: Treatment of amblyopia with esotropia involves full refractive correction using cycloplegic refraction and occlusion therapy (patching the normal eye) to stimulate the amblyopic eye.

stem: Which of the following is an adverse effect of local cycloplegics?
Which of the following is an adverse effect of local cycloplegics?
explanation_verbatim: Cycloplegic drops like atropine can cause systemic anticholinergic effects including flushing, fever, and delirium, especially in children.

stem: A 22-year-old male patient presented to the ophthalmology clinic with a complaint of seeing bugs or cobwebs together with light flashes. Ophthalmoscopy revealed an evident Weiss ring and absent red reflex. Which of the following is the best next step in the management of that patient?

A 22-year-old male patient presented to the ophthalmology clinic with a complaint of seeing bugs or cobwebs together with light flashes. Ophthalmoscopy revealed an evident Weiss ring and absent red reflex. Which of the following is the best next step in the management of that patient?
explanation_verbatim: Flashes, floaters, and a Weiss ring indicate posterior vitreous detachment, which can be associated with retinal tears. A dilated fundus exam is crucial to rule out retinal detachment.

stem: Which of the following is NOT true regarding endophthalmitis?
options: It occurs most commonly due to endogenous spread of infection
Infectious organisms are most commonly bacterial

stem: Which of the following is NOT true regarding endophthalmitis?
options: It occurs most commonly due to endogenous spread of infection
Infectious organisms are most commonly bacterial
explanation_verbatim: Endophthalmitis is usually exogenous, most commonly postoperative or post-traumatic. It’s an ophthalmic emergency requiring intravitreal antibiotics.

stem: Which of the following is NOT among the differential diagnosis of cherry red spot seen in ophthalmoscopy?
Which of the following is NOT among the differential diagnosis of cherry red spot seen in ophthalmoscopy?
explanation_verbatim: A cherry-red spot is seen in central retinal artery occlusion and certain storage diseases (e.g., Tay-Sachs, Niemann-Pick), but not in penetrating trauma.

stem: Which of the following is the leading cause of irreversible blindness in the western world?
Which of the following is the leading cause of irreversible blindness in the western world?
explanation_verbatim: AMD is the leading cause of irreversible blindness in developed countries due to degeneration of the macula affecting central vision.

stem: A 35-year-old male patient presented with floaters and blurry vision. Examination revealed snow balls and small banking. What is the best line of treatment for such a patient?
A 35-year-old male patient presented with floaters and blurry vision. Examination revealed snow balls and small banking. What is the best line of treatment for such a patient?
explanation_verbatim: Snowballs and snowbanking indicate pars planitis (intermediate uveitis). It is treated with corticosteroids, often via intravitreal or periocular injection.

stem: Which of the following is characteristic of comitant strabismus?
options: Degree of misalignment varies with gaze
Degree of misalignment is equal in all directions of gaze
Caused by orbital disease or trauma

stem: Which of the following is characteristic of comitant strabismus?
options: Degree of misalignment varies with gaze
Degree of misalignment is equal in all directions of gaze
Caused by orbital disease or trauma
explanation_verbatim: Comitant strabismus shows constant deviation in all gaze directions and is not due to muscle paralysis, often seen in childhood squint.

stem: Which of the following is a cause of vision loss in diabetic retinopathy?
Which of the following is a cause of vision loss in diabetic retinopathy?
explanation_verbatim: In diabetic retinopathy, neovascularization can rupture, causing vitreous hemorrhage and sudden loss of vision.

stem: A 34-year-old male patient presented with a complaint of dual vision especially when looking downwards. Examination revealed hypertropia, weak depression of the left eye when adducted together with chin depression and head tilt to the right side. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old male patient presented with a complaint of dual vision especially when looking downwards. Examination revealed hypertropia, weak depression of the left eye when adducted together with chin depression and head tilt to the right side. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Superior oblique palsy causes vertical diplopia, worse on looking down (e.g., reading, descending stairs), with compensatory head tilt to the opposite side.

stem: What is the best management of a diabetic patient with paralytic strabismus due to poorly-controlled DM?
options: Watchful waiting with good glycemic control for 12 months
Watchful waiting with good glycemic control for 6 months

stem: What is the best management of a diabetic patient with paralytic strabismus due to poorly-controlled DM?
options: Watchful waiting with good glycemic control for 12 months
Watchful waiting with good glycemic control for 6 months
explanation_verbatim: Diabetic cranial nerve palsy is often ischemic and resolves spontaneously within months; management focuses on blood sugar control and observation.

stem: Which of the following is the type of strabismus caused by longstanding poor vision?
Which of the following is the type of strabismus caused by longstanding poor vision?
explanation_verbatim: Poor or lost vision in one eye disrupts fusion, leading to sensory strabismus, commonly manifesting as secondary deviation of the affected eye.

stem: A 35-year-old male patient was found to have posterior uveitis as a result of an infectious process. Which of the following is the most common cause of this patient's condition?
A 35-year-old male patient was found to have posterior uveitis as a result of an infectious process. Which of the following is the most common cause of this patient's condition?
explanation_verbatim: Toxoplasmosis is the most common cause of infectious posterior uveitis, producing focal necrotizing retinochoroiditis with overlying vitreous haze (“headlight in fog”).

stem: An old hypertensive male patient developed sudden acute rise in blood pressure that was accompanied by blurred vision and large subconjunctival hemorrhage. Ophthalmoscopy revealed exudative retinal detachment. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step to be carried out in that patient?

An old hypertensive male patient developed sudden acute rise in blood pressure that was accompanied by blurred vision and large subconjunctival hemorrhage. Ophthalmoscopy revealed exudative retinal detachment. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step to be carried out in that patient?
explanation_verbatim: In hypertensive crisis with exudative retinal detachment, blood pressure must be lowered gradually to prevent optic nerve or cerebral ischemia.

stem: In the evaluation of nasolacrimal duct patency using the dye disappearance test, which of the following indicates an abnormal result?
options: Dye disappearance in more than 5 seconds
Dye disappearance in less than 5 seconds
Dye persistence for more than 5 minutes
Dye disappearance in more than 10 seconds

stem: In the evaluation of nasolacrimal duct patency using the dye disappearance test, which of the following indicates an abnormal result?
options: Dye disappearance in more than 5 seconds
Dye disappearance in less than 5 seconds
Dye persistence for more than 5 minutes
Dye disappearance in more than 10 seconds
explanation_verbatim: In the fluorescein dye disappearance test, persistence of dye >5 minutes suggests obstruction of nasolacrimal drainage.

stem: A diabetic patient with pre-existing diabetic retinopathy was informed by her ophthalmologist that she developed new blood vessel formation on retina and iris. What's the best line of management for that patient?

A diabetic patient with pre-existing diabetic retinopathy was informed by her ophthalmologist that she developed new blood vessel formation on retina and iris. What's the best line of management for that patient?
explanation_verbatim: New vessel formation on retina and iris indicates proliferative diabetic retinopathy. The treatment of choice is panretinal photocoagulation to reduce ischemic drive.

stem: A 30-year-old man got a fist blow in his right eye during a quarrel with his wife that made him feel severe eye pain. He headed to the ophthalmologist who examined his eye and found that the trauma caused hemorrhage and blood accumulation in the anterior chamber. Fluid level was sharply demarkated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man got a fist blow in his right eye during a quarrel with his wife that made him feel severe eye pain. He headed to the ophthalmologist who examined his eye and found that the trauma caused hemorrhage and blood accumulation in the anterior chamber. Fluid level was sharply demarkated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Blood in the anterior chamber forming a distinct level is diagnostic of hyphema, commonly caused by blunt trauma.

stem: A 26-year-old male presents to the emergency department after he had a severe head trauma. He complained of severe left eye pain with swelling of the left lower lid. Examination revealed limitation of ocular motility with ecchymosis and lid hematoma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old male presents to the emergency department after he had a severe head trauma. He complained of severe left eye pain with swelling of the left lower lid. Examination revealed limitation of ocular motility with ecchymosis and lid hematoma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Retrobulbar hemorrhage is a vision-threatening emergency that can follow trauma. It presents with sudden eye pain, proptosis, lid swelling, ecchymosis, and restricted ocular movement due to increased orbital pressure. Prompt recognition and intervention (e.g. lateral canthotomy) are essential to prevent optic nerve damage.

stem: What is the percentage of aqueous humor that is drained by the uveoscleral pathway?
What is the percentage of aqueous humor that is drained by the uveoscleral pathway?
explanation_verbatim: The uveoscleral pathway accounts For about 10% of aqueous humor drainage. It is an alternative route where aqueous humor flows through the ciliary muscle and exits via the suprachoroidal space. Some medications, like prostaglandin analogs, specifically enhance this pathway

stem: A 24-year-old man complains of greasy soft lash scales. History and examination revealed marked seborrheic dermatitis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 24-year-old man complains of greasy soft lash scales. History and examination revealed marked seborrheic dermatitis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Seborrheic anterior blepharitis presents with greasy soft scales on lashes and is associated with seborrheic dermatitis.

stem: Which of the following is the most important line of management of dry eye disease?
Which of the following is the most important line of management of dry eye disease?
explanation_verbatim: Although artificial tears relieve symptoms, treating the underlying cause (e.g., lid disease, systemic conditions) is most important for long-term control of dry eye.

stem: An old male patient reports an improvement in his near vision and that he no longer needs his reading glasses, however, he reports that his far vision has deteriorated. Which of the following is the name of the described phenomenon?

An old male patient reports an improvement in his near vision and that he no longer needs his reading glasses, however, he reports that his far vision has deteriorated. Which of the following is the name of the described phenomenon?
explanation_verbatim: In nuclear sclerosis cataract, the refractive index of the lens increases, causing a myopic shift. Patients temporarily experience better near vision, known as the second sight phenomenon, before overall vision worsens.

stem: A 26-year-old male patient developed anaesthesia and paraesthesia in the region of lower lid, cheek and side of nose following a severe head injury. Which of the following is the structure that fractured and caused such manifestations?

A 26-year-old male patient developed anaesthesia and paraesthesia in the region of lower lid, cheek and side of nose following a severe head injury. Which of the following is the structure that fractured and caused such manifestations?
explanation_verbatim: The infraorbital canal carries the infraorbital nerve, which supplies the lower eyelid, cheek, and side of the nose. Fracture of this canal causes anesthesia and paresthesia in these areas.

stem: A 29-year-old man complains of eye pupil constriction, eyelid drooping and diminished unilateral sweating. Which of the following is the cause of that patient's condition?
A 29-year-old man complains of eye pupil constriction, eyelid drooping and diminished unilateral sweating. Which of the following is the cause of that patient's condition?
explanation_verbatim: Ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis are features of Horner’s syndrome, caused by disruption of the sympathetic pathway. Parasympathetic lesions instead cause mydriasis.

stem: A 22-year-old girl was injured severely in a car accident. Initial examination revealed that she had high fever, lid edema and conjunctival injection. Ocular motility was reduced markedly. Also, RAPD was observed. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old girl was injured severely in a car accident. Initial examination revealed that she had high fever, lid edema and conjunctiva[ injection. Ocular motility was reduced markedly. Also, RAPD was observed. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Orbital cellulitis presents with fever, lid swelling, conjunctival congestion, restricted eye movements, and relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD). It is a serious post-traumatic or sinus-related infection requiring urgent IV antibiotics.

stem: A 25-year-old man complains of foreign body sensation in the eye coupled with tearing, redness and itching. Tear film breakup time test was performed and it was found to be 7 seconds. Based on the previous data, which of the following would be the most accurate conclusion?
options: Exclude dry eye disease since TBUT is normal
Suspect dry eye disease since TBUT is non-conclusive
Confirm dry eye disease and look for its cause since TBUT is lower than normal
Artificial tear prescription would provide definitive treatment

stem: A 25-year-old man complains of foreign body sensation in the eye coupled with tearing, redness and itching. Tear film breakup time test was performed and it was found to be 7 seconds. Based on the previous data, which of the following would be the most accurate conclusion?
options: Exclude dry eye disease since TBUT is normal
Suspect dry eye disease since TBUT is non-conclusive
Confirm dry eye disease and look for its cause since TBUT is lower than normal
Artificial tear prescription would provide definitive treatment
explanation_verbatim: A tear breakup time (TBUT) less than 10 seconds indicates tear film instability. A value of 7 seconds confirms dry eye disease and warrants investigation of underlying causes.

stem: A 46-year-old male patient complains of eye redness, itching and excessive tearing. Examination revealed inability to completely occlude the palpebral fissure. Which of the following is the term used to describe the patient's condition?

A 46-year-old male patient complains of eye redness, itching and excessive tearing. Examination revealed inability to completely occlude the palpebral fissure. Which of the following is the term used to describe the patient's condition?
explanation_verbatim: Lagophthalmos is the inability to completely close the eyelids, leading to exposure-related irritation, redness, and tearing. It may result from facial nerve palsy or eyelid scarring.

stem: A 30-year-old woman complains of acute eye redness, burning and muco purulent discharge. Upon examination, it was evident that she had conjunctival injection and chemosis and eyelid edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman complains of acute eye redness, burning and muco purulent discharge. Upon examination, it was evident that she had conjunctival injection and chemosis and eyelid edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Bacterial conjunctivitis is characterized by redness, mucopurulent discharge, eyelid edema, and conjunctival injection. It develops acutely and responds well to topical antibiotics.

stem: Which of the following is the structure responsible for secreting middle watery layer of tear film?
Which of the following is the structure responsible for secreting middle watery layer of tear film?
explanation_verbatim: The lacrimal glands secrete the watery (middle) layer of the tear film, responsible for lubrication and nutrition of the cornea. Meibomian glands secrete the lipid layer, and goblet cells produce the mucin layer.

stem: A 58-year-old male patient presents with complete lens opacification. What is the best tool used to visualize retina in that patient?
A 58-year-old male patient presents with complete lens opacification. What is the best tool used to visualize retina in that patient?
explanation_verbatim: In cases of mature or hypermature cataract, the opaque lens blocks fundus visualization. B-scan ultrasonography helps assess the retina and posterior segment structures.

stem: Which of the following conditions is among the causes of secondary angle closure glaucoma?
Which of the following conditions is among the causes of secondary angle closure glaucoma?
explanation_verbatim: Phacomorphic glaucoma results from swelling of a mature cataractous lens, narrowing the anterior chamber angle. It is a form of secondary angle-closure glaucoma.

stem: A 39-year-old male presents with unilateral miosis, eyelid drooping (ptosis), and apparent enophthalmos. Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
A 39-year-old male presents with unilateral miosis, eyelid drooping (ptosis), and apparent enophthalmos. Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Ptosis, miosis, and enophthalmos indicate Horner’s syndrome, which can be caused by a lesion anywhere along the sympathetic chain, including apical lung tumors. MRI of the thorax helps identify a Pancoast tumor.

stem: A 60-year-old male patient complains of sudden severe eye pain, redness and discharge. History revealed that he just had a cataract surgery 1 day ago. Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed that the red reflex was altered with a yellowish tint. Externally, there was associated lid edema, proptosis and corneal edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old male patient complains of sudden severe eye pain, redness and discharge. History revealed that he just had a cataract surgery 1 day ago. Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed that the red reflex was altered with a yellowish tint. Externally, there was associated lid edema, proptosis and corneal edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Postoperative endophthalmitis presents with severe pain, decreased vision, lid edema, and yellow reflex (due to pus in vitreous). It is a surgical emergency requiring intravitreal antibiotics.

stem: A 57-year-old diabetic and hypertensive male patient complained of acute painless loss of vision in his left eye. Ophthalmoscopy revealed (blood and thunder appearance) together with cotton wool spots and diffuse retinal hemorrhages. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old diabetic and hypertensive male patient complained of acute painless loss of vision in his left eye. Ophthalmoscopy revealed (blood and thunder appearance) together with cotton wool spots and diffuse retinal hemorrhages. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: CRVO causes a “blood and thunder” fundus appearance due to widespread retinal hemorrhages and venous congestion. It often occurs in hypertensive and diabetic patients.

stem: Which of the following is the most common cause of CRVO / BRVO?
Which of the following is the most common cause of CRVO / BRVO?
explanation_verbatim: Both CRVO and BRVO most commonly result from thrombosis of the retinal vein at arteriovenous crossings. Risk factors include hypertension, diabetes, and glaucoma.

stem: Which of the following is the outermost layer of the choroid?
Which of the following is the outermost layer of the choroid?
explanation_verbatim: The outermost layer of the choroid is Haller’s layer, containing large-diameter vessels. It lies external to Sattler’s layer and the choriocapillaris.

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with chronic bilateral redness, intense itching, watery discharge, small papillae on the conjunctiva, and red, scaly, dry eyelids. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 35-year-old man presents with chronic bilateral redness, intense itching, watery discharge, small papillae on the conjunctiva, and red, scaly, dry eyelids. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Atopic keratoconjunctivitis is a chronic allergic eye disease associated with eczema and dermatitis. It causes itching, tearing, small papillae, and dry, scaly eyelids.

stem: Which of the following is the most common sites of basal cell carcinoma of eyelid?
Which of the following is the most common sites of basal cell carcinoma of eyelid?
explanation_verbatim: Basal cell carcinoma most frequently affects the lower eyelid, especially the nasal side, due to maximum UV exposure. It appears as an ulcer with rolled, pearly edges and telangiectasia.

stem: Which of the following has the poorest prognosis ever?
options: Injury to eye by sulphuric acid
Injury to eye by hydrochloric acid
Injury to eye by sodium hydroxide
All have similar effect and prognosis

stem: Which of the following has the poorest prognosis ever?
options: Injury to eye by sulphuric acid
Injury to eye by hydrochloric acid
Injury to eye by sodium hydroxide
All have similar effect and prognosis
explanation_verbatim: Alkali burns (like sodium hydroxide) penetrate deeply, causing progressive tissue destruction and scarring. They have the worst prognosis compared to acid burns.

stem: Which of the following is the retinal lesion resulting from infarction of nerve fiber layer?
Which of the following is the retinal lesion resulting from infarction of nerve fiber layer?
explanation_verbatim: Soft exudates (cotton wool spots) represent localized infarction of the nerve fiber layer due to ischemia. They appear as fluffy white patches on the retina.

stem: Which of the following is the most common use of hyperosmotic agents?
Which of the following is the most common use of hyperosmotic agents?
explanation_verbatim: Hyperosmotic agents (like mannitol) are used in acute angle-closure glaucoma to rapidly lower intraocular pressure by drawing fluid out of the vitreous.

stem: Ocular signs that manifest in patients with multiple sclerosis include all of the following except?
Ocular signs that manifest in patients with multiple sclerosis include all of the following except?
explanation_verbatim: Multiple sclerosis causes optic neuritis, RAPD, and nystagmus due to demyelination, but not peripheral scotoma. Scotomas are more typical of retinal disease or glaucoma.

stem: Which of the following is the innermost layer of the choroid?
Which of the following is the innermost layer of the choroid?
explanation_verbatim: Bruch’s membrane is the innermost layer of the choroid, lying between the choriocapillaris and retinal pigment epithelium. It plays a key role in retinal metabolism and waste transport.

stem: What is the drug that is used to treat resistant cases of vernal keratoconjunctivitis?
What is the drug that is used to treat resistant cases of vernal keratoconjunctivitis?
explanation_verbatim: In resistant cases of vernal keratoconjunctivitis, topical tacrolimus, an immunomodulator, is used when antihistamines or mast cell stabilizers fail. It suppresses local immune-mediated inflammation.

stem: What is the grade of hypertensive retinopathy characterized by (obvious arterial narrowing with focal irregularities)?
What is the grade of hypertensive retinopathy characterized by (obvious arterial narrowing with focal irregularities)?
explanation_verbatim: Grade 2 hypertensive retinopathy is characterized by obvious arterial narrowing with focal irregularities (arteriovenous nipping). It reflects moderate vascular sclerosis due to sustained hypertension.

stem: A middle-aged man complains of blurred near vision. His right eye was found to be +3 while his left eye was +2. What is the position of the far point in that patient?
A middle-aged man complains of blurred near vision. His right eye was found to be +3 while his left eye was +2. What is the position of the far point in that patient?
explanation_verbatim: In hypermetropia (farsightedness), parallel light rays focus behind the retina, hence the far point lies behind the eye. Convex lenses are used for correction.

stem: A 65-year-old man presents with sudden painless severe monocular vision loss. Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed cherry red spots together with venous stasis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man presents with sudden painless severe monocular vision loss. Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed cherry red spots together with venous stasis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: CRAO causes sudden, painless, severe vision loss with a pale retina and a cherry-red spot at the macula. It is an ophthalmic emergency due to retinal ischemia.

stem: A 38-year-old male patient complains of eye pain, excessive tearing and redness. History is significant for severe unilateral facial pain that was followed by appearance of skin vesicles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old male patient complains of eye pain, excessive tearing and redness. History is significant for severe unilateral facial pain that was followed by appearance of skin vesicles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Reactivation of varicella-zoster virus in the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve causes Herpes zoster ophthalmicus. It presents with facial pain, vesicular rash, and ocular inflammation.

stem: Which of the following is the gold-standard method for IOP measurement?
Which of the following is the gold-standard method for IOP measurement?
explanation_verbatim: The Goldmann applanation tonometer is the gold standard for intraocular pressure measurement, based on flattening a fixed corneal area. It provides the most accurate and reproducible readings.

stem: Which of the following actions is performed by the superior rectus muscle?
Which of the following actions is performed by the superior rectus muscle?
explanation_verbatim: The superior rectus muscle primarily elevates the eye and also contributes to adduction and intorsion. Its actions depend on the position of the eyeball relative to the visual axis.

stem: A 65-year-old man presents with a sudden, painless loss of vision in his right eye that lasted for a few minutes and then spontaneously resolved. He has a history of hypertension and carotid artery disease. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man presents with a sudden, painless loss of vision in his right eye that lasted for a few minutes and then spontaneously resolved. He has a history of hypertension and carotid artery disease. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Amaurosis fugax is a transient monocular blindness due to embolic occlusion from carotid artery disease. It resolves spontaneously within minutes but indicates risk of stroke.

stem: Which of the following is the among the side effects that accompany the use of local anaesthetics?
Which of the following is the among the side effects that accompany the use of local anaesthetics?
explanation_verbatim: Prolonged or excessive use of local anesthetic eye drops can cause corneal toxicity, leading to epithelial defects and delayed healing.

stem: A 66-year-old woman presents with a complaint of acutely diminished vision in the left eye coupled with severe pain the left temporal region. Examination revealed tender and cord-like texture of temporal artery on palpation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old woman presents with a complaint of acutely diminished vision in the left eye coupled with severe pain the left temporal region. Examination revealed tender and cord-like texture of temporal artery on palpation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Giant cell arteritis causes temporal artery tenderness, headache, and sudden vision loss due to ischemic optic neuropathy. It is an emergency requiring immediate corticosteroid therapy.

stem: A 59-year-old male patient visits the ophthalmologist with a complaint of a lid ulcer. He reported that the ulcer appeared 5 weeks ago and enlarged in size over that period. Examination revealed an ulcerative lesion with beaded edges and dilated vessels on the ulcer margin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old male patient visits the ophthalmologist with a complaint of a lid ulcer. He reported that the ulcer appeared 5 weeks ago and enlarged in size over that period. Examination revealed an ulcerative lesion with beaded edges and dilated vessels on the ulcer margin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Basal cell carcinoma presents as a slow-growing ulcer with rolled, beaded edges and dilated vessels. It is the most common malignant eyelid tumor.

explanation_verbatim: AION presents with sudden, painless vision loss and a swollen pale optic disc with hemorrhages. It is due to ischemia of the optic nerve head, often linked to hypertension or diabetes.

A 61-year-old woman complains of seeing straight objects as if they were wavy. History was taken and it showed that the patient was a heavy smoker. Ophthalmoscopy revealed drusen formation. Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Metamorphopsia (seeing straight lines as wavy) with drusen formation is characteristic of age-related macular degeneration. Smoking is a major risk factor, and the macula is primarily affected, leading to central vision loss.

stem: In iridocyclitis, which of the following is the expected change that will occur in intraocular pressure?
options: It may either decrease or increase
explanation_verbatim: In iridocyclitis (anterior uveitis), intraocular pressure (IOP) may initially decrease due to reduced aqueous humor production from ciliary body inflammation, but later increase due to blockage of the trabecular meshwork by inflammatory cells. Thus, IOP changes are variable.

explanation_verbatim: A carotid-cavernous fistula typically presents with pulsating exophthalmos, conjunctival congestion, and a bruit following head trauma. It results from an abnormal communication between the carotid artery and cavernous sinus.

explanation_verbatim: The described features (foamy discharge, lid margin hyperemia, telangiectasia) indicate meibomian gland dysfunction (posterior blepharitis). It results from thickened, stagnant secretions obstructing gland ducts.

explanation_verbatim: A painless swelling at the inner canthus with tearing indicates chronic dacryocystitis. It is due to nasolacrimal duct obstruction, causing chronic infection and mucus retention in the lacrimal sac.

stem: Which of the following best describes Morgagnian Cataract ?

It's a form of hypermature cataract with lens cortex liquefaction causing the dark nucleus to sink inferiorly inside the lens capsule

stem: Which of the following is true regarding comitant strabismus?
options: Misalignment varies with direction of gaze

explanation_verbatim: In comitant strabismus, the angle of deviation remains constant in all directions of gaze because the extraocular muscles function normally. It is typically congenital or developmental, not neurologic.

stem: Accommodation of the eye can be achieved by:
options: changing the antero-posterior diameter of the eye.

increasing the depth of the anterior chamber.
explanation_verbatim: Accommodation occurs when the ciliary muscle contracts, relaxing the zonular fibers and allowing the lens to become more convex. This increases its refractive power for near vision.

stem: A small intraocular iron foreign body:
options: can be left if it doesn’t harm the eye.
can only be removed if it produces cataract
explanation_verbatim: Even a small intraocular iron foreign body must be removed because iron causes siderosis bulbi—toxic degeneration of ocular tissues. Leaving it in place risks permanent visual damage.
